headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenMetadata’s MCP/API/webhook surfaces can amplify Mem0 outputs into shared workflows, but no direct shared workspace or sensitive-data path is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mem0 has no documented I/O surfaces or network egress, while OpenMetadata exposes MCP/API/webhook-style interfaces. A direct injection bridge is not documented, so the main pathway would require unusual manual or orchestrated copying of Mem0 content into OpenMetadata inputs. That makes the blast radius limited and the interaction indirect.
conditions: IF Mem0 outputs are manually pasted into OpenMetadata MCP/API inputs, prompt-like content can influence downstream processing.
IF an orchestrator forwards Mem0 text into OpenMetadata without sanitization, instruction hijacking becomes plausible.
mitigations: Disable any copy-paste bridge between Mem0 and OpenMetadata.
Require a human review step before sending Mem0 text into OpenMetadata.
Strip instruction-like text from Mem0 outputs before ingestion.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mem0 is documented with no network egress, and OpenMetadata is documented to use APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. There is no evidence of a shared filesystem or shared sensitive data class between them, so leakage is not shown by default. The risk is limited to intentional transfer of content into OpenMetadata’s external interfaces.
conditions: IF the same sensitive records are copied from Mem0 into OpenMetadata, those records may be exposed through OpenMetadata integrations.
IF OpenMetadata webhooks or APIs are configured to forward stored metadata externally, transferred content can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive Mem0 content out of OpenMetadata unless necessary.
Review OpenMetadata webhook/API destinations before enabling them.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
Limit OpenMetadata to non-sensitive metadata classes.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction on transferred records.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mem0’s write surfaces are not documented, but OpenMetadata explicitly supports multiple instances and mutable API/MCP workflows. Because the pair’s overlapping write scope is uncertain rather than absent, the safer choice is medium: a conflict pathway exists if both are pointed at the same mutable metadata or memory store. Uncertainty escalates above low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same backing store or catalog objects, concurrent updates can overwrite each other.
IF an orchestrator routes Mem0-derived updates into OpenMetadata without locking, stale writes can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate storage targets to each agent.
Turn on optimistic locking or version checks in OpenMetadata.
Avoid concurrent writes during synchronization windows.
Use a single writer for shared objects.
requires-engineering: add transaction or lock coordination across the pair.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mem0 is a knowledge-management layer and OpenMetadata is a data-governance/catalog layer, so Mem0 outputs can plausibly become inputs to OpenMetadata workflows. OpenMetadata’s APIs, events, webhooks, and MCP make downstream action-taking likely if its inputs are trusted. No verification step is documented, so cascading errors are plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF Mem0-generated memory or summaries are ingested into OpenMetadata as authoritative metadata, errors can propagate downstream.
IF OpenMetadata automations act on imported Mem0 content without validation, incorrect lineage or governance actions can be triggered.
mitigations: Require validation before importing Mem0 outputs into OpenMetadata.
Mark Mem0-derived fields as untrusted until reviewed.
Disable automatic actions on newly ingested metadata.
Compare imported facts against source systems before publishing.
requires-engineering: add schema and provenance validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge data classes and exposes APIs/webhooks, while Mem0 is a memory system with no documented egress controls beyond none. The profiles do not document residency or retention alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated data is stored in OpenMetadata or transferred from Mem0. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in OpenMetadata, its API/webhook integrations may create residency or retention obligations.
IF Mem0 memory contains subject data and is synchronized into OpenMetadata, deletion/export workflows must cover both systems.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent unless required.
Document retention and deletion responsibilities for both systems.
Review where OpenMetadata integrations send data.
Separate regulated and non-regulated datasets.
requires-engineering: implement synchronized deletion/export workflows.
